findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "canvas_open" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: search, get_details, check_conditions, verify_answer · Private data: search · Public sink: search, cost_scenarios, share_ranking · Destructive: search, check_conditions, share_ranking, relax_conditions, canvas_do.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: search, get_details, check_conditions, verify_answer · Private data: search · Public sink: search, cost_scenarios, share_ranking · Destructive: search, check_conditions, share_ranking, relax_conditions, canvas_do

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "search" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
